standard_prerequisites.use: Noetherian schemes of finite type, completions of local rings at their maximal ideal, base change of a morphism along a formal local map, and conormal algebras of closed immersions cut out by such base changes. The control construction and the comparison of conormal algebras are retained.

core_obligations: Construct the finite type modification (T',t') -> (T,t) through which sigma factors, uniformly for all local O_{S,s}-algebra maps sigma' that factor through it.
Show that for every such sigma' the two closed immersions Y_sigma <- Y_t -> Y_sigma' have isomorphic conormal algebras, which is the graded content beyond the ungraded control statement.

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the composable finite type situation Y -> T -> S with t mapping to s and the local map sigma, and build the finite type modification T' controlling sigma.
Compare the two base changes Y_sigma and Y_sigma' along the formal maps and identify the conormal algebras of the resulting closed immersions Y_sigma <- Y_t -> Y_sigma'.

difficulty_reason: This is the graded companion of the Artin approximation control step. Over a composable pair Y -> T -> S of finite type Noetherian schemes and a local O_{S,s}-algebra map sigma : O_{T,t} -> O_{S,s}^, the lemma produces a single finite type modification (T',t') -> (T,t) through which sigma factors, such that every other sigma' factoring through it induces closed immersions Y_sigma <- Y_t -> Y_sigma' with isomorphic conormal algebras. The proof has to compare two base changes of Y along two different formal maps that agree through the modification, then transport the conormal algebra across the comparison; the uniformity in sigma' is what carries the content, since a single modification must serve all competitors at once. The graded statement is not implied by the ungraded control lemma in any routine way, because conormal algebras of the two closed immersions, not just the maps, must match. Retained author proof at lines 11592-11718.
